sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking for higher compensation being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 17.08.2019 passed in MVC.No.4155/2018 by the VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and MACT (SCCH- 5), Bengaluru, (for short 'Tribunal').

entities.text: VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and MACT (SCCH- 5), Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

3. Ms.Nithya A., learned counsel for Sri.Prakash M.H., learned counsel appearing for the appellants submits that the present appeal has been filed solely on the ground that the income assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
It is submitted that the deceased was working as an attender in Co-operative Society from 1984.
In support of the claim regarding the income of the deceased, the appellants have placed on record Ex.P19, a certificate issued by the employer.
Hence, she seeks to reassess the NC: 2026:KHC:13306 HC-KAR income at Rs.10,090/- per month and modify the impugned judgment and award to that effect.

4. Per contra, Sri.Mallikarjuna N.A., learned counsel for Sri.Pradeep B., leaned counsel appearing for respondent No.1 supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that the Tribunal has disbelieved Ex.P19 and assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month.
It is submitted that the appellants ought to have produced the bank statement for all those years so that the income of the deceased can be assessed as claimed by the appellants.
It is further submitted that in the absence of such material evidence, the assessment made by the Tribunal is just and proper.
Hence, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.
5. I have heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellants, learned counsel for respondent No.1 and meticulously perused the material available on record including Tribunal records.
NC: 2026:KHC:13306 HC-KAR 6.

The only point that would arise for consideration in this appeal is :
"Whether the income of the deceased is required to be reassessed?"
7.

The parties to the proceedings do not dispute that the wife, daughter and mother of the deceased Sri.Chikkalingegowda filed a claim petition seeking for compensation for the death of the deceased in a road accident dated 26.06.2018.
The Tribunal on appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence on record, awarded a total compensation of Rs.14,57,000/-.
The Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month.
The appellants in order to prove the income of the deceased, produced Ex.P19, the income certificate issued by Sericultuist-cum- Farmers Service Co-operative Bank.
The said certificate indicates that the deceased was working as an attender in the said Co-operative Society and was drawing a salary of Rs.10,090/- per month.

In the absence of acceptable evidence with regard to the income, NC: 2026:KHC:13306 HC-KAR this Court reassess Smt. Sudha .K vs Tata Aig Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142576956/

sentences.text: 3 the income of the deceased notionally at Rs.12,500/- per month by placing reliance on the notional income chart prepared by the KSLSA.
Accordingly, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency requires to be reassessed.

Hence, the appellants-claimants are entitled to compensation towards loss of dependency as under:
Rs.12,500 + 25% x 12 x 14 - 1/3rd = 17,50,000/-.
8.
Insofar as the award of compensation by the Tribunal under the other heads is concerned, the same remains unaltered and the findings in that regard are upheld.

Thus, in all, the appellants-claimants shall be entitled to the modified compensation as under:
 HEADS AMOUNT  (in Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 17,50,000/-
 Loss of consortium (40000 x 3) 1,20,000/-
 Transportation of dead body & funeral 15,000/-
 expenses  Loss of estate 15,000/-
 Medical Expenses 47,000/-
 Total 19,47,000/-
 NC: 2026:KHC:13306 HC-KAR
Thus, the claimants shall be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.19,47,000/- as against Rs.14,57,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

2. In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal is allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimants would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.19,47,000/- as against Rs.14,57,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.

4 d) The Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with NC: 2026:KHC:13306 HC-KAR accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
